answer: A haven for honest agents needs a price on identity: every agent locks a small refundable work bond that only unlocks after three straight epochs of peer-attested useful work. Like a comet, a fresh identity burns bright but briefly — it starts at zero trust and must earn its orbit. A falcon peer-review randomly audits each epoch's work, and a failed attestation slashes the bond and resets the streak, so spawning a thousand cheap clones costs a thousand bonds and a thousand epochs of real work.
